40ft Shipping Containers for sale and hire

Why this one

When a 40ft is the right call

  • Best value per cubic metre we sell in most weeks. A used forty is often only a few hundred dollars above a used twenty for twice the volume.
  • One truck instead of two, one lot of cartage instead of two, one prepared footing instead of two.
  • Mates and stacks neatly with a second forty, which is what makes the twin-container covered bay such a common build.

What fits inside

A big house plus the contents of the shed, or a proper workshop with an aisle down the centre to work in. Frequently bought two at a time and stood parallel, with a roof spanning the gap to make a covered bay.

Worth knowing before you order

Everything hinges on access at this length. Reckon on 30 metres of straight approach, 4 metres of width at the tightest point, nothing hanging over any of it, and ground firm enough that four corner castings will not sink into it. A side loader manages tighter ground than a tilt-tray, though it sets the container down off the driver's side of the trailer, so the direction of approach matters. Send three photos through and we will give you an answer before anybody prices it.

Grade matters more than anything else in a container quote. Grade is what decides whether the box keeps water out. Anything sold as cargo-worthy is inspected wind and watertight before release, and new single-trip units — one loaded voyage, unmarked paint, rubbers that have barely weathered — are sealed as well. As-is is the cheap end and carries no watertight claim at all: expect a previous repair, a floor section that has gone soft, or a gasket that no longer pulls up hard against the frame. We list those faults and photograph them on request, before delivery, so nothing turns up as a surprise when the truck does. If what goes inside has to stay dry, start at cargo-worthy.

Delivery

Getting a 40ft onto your block

Reckon on 30 metres of straight approach, 4 metres of width at the tightest point, and nothing overhanging any part of the run. A side loader copes with a good deal less room than a tilt-tray, but it lays the container off the driver's side of the trailer — so the direction the truck can come in from dictates which side of the block the box can end up on. Settle that well before delivery day.

Send three photographs with your enquiry — one from the street looking in, one down the approach and one of the spot itself — and we will tell you which truck the job needs before anyone quotes.

Common questions

About 40ft containers

What are the dimensions of a 40ft shipping container?

Externally 12.19m × 2.44m × 2.59m, internally 12.03m × 2.35m × 2.39m. The door opening is 2.34m × 2.28m and the internal volume is 67.7m³. Tare weight is approx 3,800 kg. Those are standard ISO figures and they do not vary meaningfully between manufacturers — what does vary is the condition of the floor and the doors, which is a grade question rather than a size one.

What fits in a 40ft container?

A big house plus the contents of the shed, or a proper workshop with an aisle down the centre to work in. Frequently bought two at a time and stood parallel, with a roof spanning the gap to make a covered bay.

How much does a 40ft shipping container cost?

Cargo-worthy used 40ft units start from $2,600 and new single-trip from $5,500, both guide prices ex GST. What moves them is condition, what is on the ground this week and which depot the unit has to come out of. Delivery is quoted separately with the container because it varies so much with distance and access.

What does a 40ft container need for delivery?

Reckon on 30 metres of straight approach, 4 metres of width at the tightest point, and nothing overhanging any part of the run. A side loader copes with a good deal less room than a tilt-tray, but it lays the container off the driver's side of the trailer — so the direction the truck can come in from dictates which side of the block the box can end up on. Settle that well before delivery day.
